1 Samuel.line: Israel moves from the judges to kingship through Samuel the prophet, the failed reign of Saul, and the rise of David.
more: Hannah prays for a son, and God gives her Samuel, who grows up serving at the tabernacle in Shiloh.
Eli's corrupt house falls, the Philistines capture the ark, and Samuel leads Israel as judge and prophet.
Israel demands a king, and Samuel anoints Saul, who soon disobeys God and is rejected.
God chooses young David, who kills Goliath and becomes a hero but is hunted by the jealous Saul.
David spares Saul twice while living as a fugitive, and Saul finally dies in battle against the Philistines.

1.line: Barren Hannah prays at Shiloh for a son, and God gives her Samuel, whom she gives back to the LORD.
more: Hannah is one of Elkanah's two wives and is taunted by Peninnah, who has children.
Eli the priest first thinks she is drunk, then blesses her request.
After weaning Samuel, Hannah brings him to Eli to serve the LORD for life.

2.line: Hannah praises God in a song, while Eli's sons sin openly and a prophet announces judgment on Eli's house.
more: Hannah's song celebrates God humbling the proud and lifting up the lowly.
Hophni and Phinehas take the best of the sacrifices by force and sleep with women serving at the tabernacle.
Young Samuel grows in favor, and a man of God says both of Eli's sons will die on one day.

3.line: God calls the boy Samuel by name at night and reveals that judgment is coming on Eli's family.
more: Samuel thinks Eli is calling him until Eli realizes the LORD is speaking.
Eli accepts the message, and all Israel comes to recognize Samuel as a prophet.

4.line: The Philistines defeat Israel, capture the ark of God, and kill Eli's sons, and Eli dies on hearing the news.
more: Israel brings the ark into battle hoping it will save them, but suffers a heavy defeat.
Eli falls backward and breaks his neck when told the ark is taken.
Phinehas's wife dies in childbirth, naming her son Ichabod because the glory has departed.

5.line: The captured ark brings disaster on the Philistines, as their idol Dagon falls and tumors strike their cities.
more: Dagon's statue is found fallen before the ark, then found broken.
The ark is moved from Ashdod to Gath to Ekron, and plague follows it everywhere.

6.line: The Philistines send the ark back on a cart with guilt offerings, and it returns to Israel at Beth-shemesh.
more: Two milk cows pull the cart straight to Israel's border without a driver.
Some men of Beth-shemesh look into the ark and are struck down.
The ark is then sent on to Kiriath-jearim.

7.line: Samuel calls Israel to repent and put away idols, and God routs the Philistines at Mizpah.
more: The ark remains at Kiriath-jearim for twenty years.
God thunders against the Philistines while Samuel offers a sacrifice, and Samuel sets up a stone named Ebenezer.
Samuel judges Israel all his life, traveling a yearly circuit.

8.line: Israel demands a king like the other nations, and God tells Samuel to grant it after warning them.
more: Samuel's sons take bribes, prompting the elders' request.
God says the people are rejecting him as king, not Samuel.
Samuel warns that a king will take their sons, land, and goods, but they insist.

9.line: While searching for lost donkeys, Saul meets Samuel, whom God has told to anoint him as Israel's leader.
more: Saul is a tall, handsome Benjaminite, the son of Kish.
Samuel honors Saul at a feast and keeps him overnight.

10.line: Samuel anoints Saul privately, signs confirm it, and Saul is then publicly chosen king by lot at Mizpah.
more: God gives Saul another heart, and he prophesies with a group of prophets.
At Mizpah Saul is found hiding among the baggage.
Some worthless men despise him, but Saul keeps silent.

11.line: Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead from the Ammonites, and the people renew his kingship at Gilgal.
more: Nahash the Ammonite threatens to gouge out the right eye of every man in Jabesh.
The Spirit of God rushes on Saul, and he rallies Israel to a decisive victory.
Saul refuses to punish those who had doubted him.

12.line: Samuel gives a farewell speech, defends his integrity, and urges Israel and its king to fear and serve the LORD.
more: Samuel reviews God's faithfulness from Egypt through the judges.
God sends thunder and rain at wheat harvest, and the people confess that asking for a king was evil.
Samuel promises to keep praying for them and warns that persistent wickedness will bring ruin.

13.line: Facing the Philistines at Gilgal, Saul offers a sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel and loses his dynasty.
more: Jonathan attacks a Philistine garrison, and the Philistines gather a huge army.
Samuel says God will seek a man after his own heart.
Israel has almost no swords, because the Philistines control metalworking.

14.line: Jonathan and his armor-bearer attack a Philistine outpost, God sends panic, and Israel wins a great victory.
more: Saul's rash oath forbids eating, and Jonathan unknowingly tastes honey.
The hungry troops eat meat with the blood, and Saul builds an altar.
The people save Jonathan from Saul's death sentence, and Saul fights enemies on every side.

15.line: Saul spares King Agag and the best Amalekite livestock against God's command, and God rejects him as king.
more: Saul claims the animals were kept for sacrifice, but Samuel says obedience is better than sacrifice.
Saul tears Samuel's robe, and Samuel says the kingdom has been torn from Saul.
Samuel kills Agag, departs, and grieves over Saul.

16.line: God sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint David, Jesse's youngest son, and David enters Saul's service as a musician.
more: God tells Samuel that he looks on the heart, not outward appearance.
The Spirit rushes on David and departs from Saul, and a harmful spirit torments Saul.
David's lyre playing brings Saul relief, and he becomes Saul's armor-bearer.

17.line: The young shepherd David kills the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and stone, and Israel routs the Philistines.
more: Goliath defies Israel's army for forty days, and Saul's soldiers are afraid.
David, bringing food to his brothers, volunteers, trusting the LORD who saved him from lion and bear.
He refuses Saul's armor and cuts off Goliath's head with the giant's own sword.

18.line: Jonathan loves David as himself, but Saul grows jealous of David's success and tries to kill him.
more: Women sing that Saul has killed thousands but David tens of thousands.
Saul hurls a spear at David and sends him into dangerous battles.
David marries Saul's daughter Michal after killing two hundred Philistines as the bride-price.

19.line: Saul openly seeks to kill David, who escapes with help from Jonathan and Michal and flees to Samuel.
more: Jonathan briefly reconciles them, but Saul throws a spear at David again.
Michal lets David down through a window and puts an idol in his bed.
At Ramah, Saul's messengers and Saul himself are overcome by the Spirit and prophesy.

20.line: Jonathan confirms Saul's intent to kill David, and the two friends part after renewing their covenant.
more: David misses the new moon feast, and Saul angrily throws a spear at Jonathan.
Jonathan signals David with arrows in the field, as agreed.
They weep and swear loyalty to each other's descendants.

21.line: Fleeing, David gets holy bread and Goliath's sword from the priest at Nob, then pretends to be insane in Gath.
more: Ahimelech the priest gives David the consecrated bread.
Doeg the Edomite, Saul's servant, witnesses this.
King Achish of Gath dismisses David as a madman.

22.line: David gathers men at the cave of Adullam, while Saul has Doeg slaughter the priests of Nob.
more: About four hundred distressed, indebted, and bitter men join David.
David places his parents under the protection of the king of Moab.
Only Abiathar escapes the massacre and joins David.

23.line: David rescues Keilah from the Philistines, then barely escapes Saul in the wilderness.
more: David inquires of God through the ephod and learns Keilah would hand him over.
Jonathan visits David at Horesh and strengthens his hand in God.
Saul nearly traps David but leaves to fight a Philistine raid.

24.line: David spares Saul in a cave at En-gedi, cutting off a corner of his robe instead of killing him.
more: David refuses to harm the LORD's anointed.
Saul weeps, admits David is more righteous, and asks him to spare his descendants.

25.line: Wise Abigail keeps David from taking revenge on her foolish husband Nabal, who then dies, and she marries David.
more: Samuel dies and all Israel mourns him.
Nabal rudely refuses provisions to David's men, who had protected his shepherds.
About ten days later the LORD strikes Nabal and he dies.

26.line: David again spares Saul, taking his spear and water jar while Saul sleeps in the camp.
more: Abishai offers to kill Saul, but David refuses.
From a distance David rebukes Abner for failing to guard the king.
Saul confesses his wrong and blesses David, and they part.

27.line: Despairing of escaping Saul, David settles among the Philistines and receives the town of Ziklag from Achish.
more: Saul stops pursuing him.
David raids Israel's enemies but tells Achish he is raiding Judah.
He leaves no survivors so the truth will not reach Achish.

28.line: With the Philistines gathering, Saul consults a medium at En-dor, and Samuel announces Saul's defeat and death.
more: God no longer answers Saul by dreams, Urim, or prophets.
Saul had earlier banished mediums from the land.
Samuel says Saul and his sons will die the next day.

29.line: The Philistine commanders distrust David, so Achish sends him back from the battle against Israel.
more: They fear David will turn against them in battle.
Achish insists David has been loyal but yields to them.

30.line: David finds Ziklag burned and families taken by Amalekites, then pursues them and recovers everything.
more: David's men talk of stoning him, but he strengthens himself in the LORD.
An abandoned Egyptian servant leads David to the raiders.
David rules that those guarding supplies share equally, and he sends spoil to Judah's elders.

31.line: Saul and three of his sons, including Jonathan, die in battle with the Philistines on Mount Gilboa.
more: Badly wounded, Saul falls on his own sword.
The Philistines fasten the bodies to the wall of Beth-shan.
Men of Jabesh-gilead recover the bodies and bury them.

2 Samuel.line: David becomes king over Judah and then all Israel, receives God's covenant promise, but sins grievously and faces family turmoil.
more: David mourns Saul and Jonathan and is anointed king of Judah at Hebron.
After war with Saul's house, he rules all Israel, captures Jerusalem, and brings the ark there.
God promises David a house and a kingdom that will last forever.
David commits adultery with Bathsheba and arranges Uriah's death, and Nathan announces trouble within his house.
Amnon's crime, Absalom's revolt, and Sheba's rebellion follow, but David is restored to the throne.
The book closes with accounts of a famine, warriors, songs, and a census followed by plague.

1.line: An Amalekite reports Saul's death and claims credit, and David has him executed and laments Saul and Jonathan.
more: The Amalekite brings Saul's crown and armlet to David at Ziklag.
David's lament, the Song of the Bow, mourns how the mighty have fallen.

2.line: David is anointed king of Judah at Hebron, while Abner makes Saul's son Ish-bosheth king over Israel.
more: David thanks the men of Jabesh-gilead for burying Saul.
At Gibeon, Joab's men defeat Abner's men.
Abner kills Joab's brother Asahel, who was chasing him.

3.line: Abner breaks with Ish-bosheth and joins David, but Joab murders him in revenge, and David mourns Abner publicly.
more: David's house grows stronger while Saul's grows weaker, and sons are born to David in Hebron.
Abner quarrels with Ish-bosheth over Saul's concubine and offers Israel to David.
David demands Michal's return and curses Joab's house for the killing.

4.line: Two captains murder Ish-bosheth in his bed and bring his head to David, who executes them.
more: Jonathan's son Mephibosheth had been crippled in a fall as a child.
Rechab and Baanah expect a reward but are punished for killing a righteous man.

5.line: David is anointed king over all Israel, captures Jerusalem from the Jebusites, and defeats the Philistines twice.
more: David reigns forty years, seven and a half in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
Hiram king of Tyre builds David a palace.
David inquires of the LORD before each battle and follows his instructions.

6.line: David brings the ark to Jerusalem after Uzzah dies for touching it, and Michal despises David's dancing.
more: The ark stays three months with Obed-edom, whose household is blessed.
David dances before the LORD with all his might, wearing a linen ephod.
Michal has no child to the day of her death.

7.line: God declines David's plan to build him a house, instead promising David an everlasting house, kingdom, and throne.
more: The prophet Nathan delivers the message.
David's son will build the temple, and God will be a father to him.
David responds with a humble prayer of thanks.

8.line: David defeats surrounding nations, including Philistia, Moab, Zobah, Syria, and Edom, as the LORD gives him victory everywhere.
more: David dedicates the plunder to the LORD.
He administers justice and equity, and his officials are listed.

9.line: David shows kindness to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, restoring Saul's land and giving him a place at the king's table.
more: David asks whether anyone of Saul's house remains, for Jonathan's sake.
Ziba, Saul's servant, is assigned to farm the land for Mephibosheth.

10.line: The Ammonites humiliate David's envoys and hire Syrian troops, and Joab and David defeat both.
more: King Hanun shaves half the envoys' beards and cuts their garments.
Joab and Abishai split the army to face the Syrians and Ammonites.
David defeats Hadadezer's forces at Helam, and the Syrians make peace.

11.line: David commits adultery with Bathsheba and, when she becomes pregnant, has her husband Uriah killed in battle.
more: David stays in Jerusalem while the army besieges Rabbah.
Uriah refuses to go home to his wife while the army is in the field.
David marries Bathsheba, but what he has done displeases the LORD.

12.line: Nathan confronts David with a parable, David repents, and the child dies, but Solomon is later born.
more: Nathan says the sword will never depart from David's house.
God names Solomon Jedidiah, meaning beloved of the LORD.
David completes the capture of Rabbah.

13.line: Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar, and her brother Absalom has him killed two years later and flees.
more: Jonadab helps Amnon plan the deception.
David is angry but does not punish Amnon.
Absalom flees to Geshur and stays three years.

14.line: Joab uses a wise woman from Tekoa to persuade David to bring Absalom home.
more: Absalom lives in Jerusalem two years without seeing the king.
He sets Joab's field on fire to get his attention.
David finally receives Absalom and kisses him.

15.line: Absalom wins the people's hearts and declares himself king in Hebron, and David flees Jerusalem.
more: Ittai the Gittite insists on going with David.
David sends the ark back with Zadok and Abiathar.
Hushai returns to Jerusalem to counter Ahithophel's advice.

16.line: As David flees, Ziba slanders Mephibosheth, Shimei curses David, and Absalom sleeps with his father's concubines.
more: David gives Ziba all of Mephibosheth's property.
David forbids Abishai to kill Shimei, saying the LORD may have told him to curse.
Hushai gains Absalom's trust, and Absalom follows Ahithophel's counsel.

17.line: Hushai's counsel defeats Ahithophel's, giving David time to escape across the Jordan, and Ahithophel hangs himself.
more: Ahithophel had urged an immediate attack on the weary king.
Jonathan and Ahimaaz carry warnings to David, hiding in a well along the way.
Barzillai and others bring supplies to David at Mahanaim.

18.line: David's forces defeat Absalom's army, and Joab kills Absalom after he is caught in a tree.
more: David orders his commanders to deal gently with Absalom.
Absalom's head catches in an oak as his mule runs on.
David weeps bitterly at the news, crying out for his son.

19.line: Joab rebukes David's grief, and David returns to Jerusalem, pardoning Shimei, while Israel and Judah quarrel over the king.
more: David replaces Joab with Amasa as commander.
Mephibosheth explains his absence, and David divides the land between him and Ziba.
Aged Barzillai declines to come to Jerusalem and sends Chimham instead.

20.line: Sheba son of Bichri leads a rebellion, and Joab murders Amasa, then ends the revolt at Abel.
more: A wise woman of Abel persuades the town to throw Sheba's head over the wall.
David's officials are listed again.

21.line: David avenges Saul's killing of the Gibeonites to end a famine, and his warriors defeat Philistine giants.
more: Seven of Saul's descendants are handed over and put to death.
Rizpah guards their bodies, and David buries the bones of Saul and Jonathan.
Abishai saves an exhausted David, and David's men kill four giants of Gath.

22.line: David sings a song of praise to the LORD for rescuing him from all his enemies and from Saul.
more: God is pictured as his rock, fortress, and deliverer.
The song closely parallels Psalm 18.
It closes with God's steadfast love to David and his offspring forever.

23.line: David's last words praise God's everlasting covenant, followed by a list of his mighty men and their deeds.
more: The three chief warriors are Josheb-basshebeth, Eleazar, and Shammah.
Three men break through Philistine lines for water from Bethlehem, which David pours out.
Uriah the Hittite is listed among the thirty.

24.line: David sinfully takes a census, God sends a plague, and David buys Araunah's threshing floor and sacrifices there.
more: David chooses to fall into God's hands rather than man's.
Seventy thousand die before the angel is stopped at Jerusalem.
David refuses to offer the LORD what costs him nothing.

1 Kings.line: Solomon's glorious reign and temple give way to a divided kingdom, as most kings of Israel and Judah turn from the LORD.
more: Solomon secures the throne, asks God for wisdom, and builds and dedicates the temple in Jerusalem.
His many foreign wives turn his heart to idols, and God promises to tear away most of the kingdom.
Under Rehoboam the ten northern tribes split off and follow Jeroboam, who sets up golden calves.
A series of kings follows, each judged by whether he did right or evil in the LORD's sight.
Elijah confronts King Ahab and Baal worship, and Ahab dies in battle as prophesied.

1.line: As David ages, Adonijah claims the throne, but Nathan and Bathsheba persuade David to make Solomon king.
more: Abishag is brought to care for the elderly David.
Joab and Abiathar support Adonijah, while Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah support Solomon.
Solomon is anointed at Gihon, and Adonijah's guests scatter in fear.

2.line: David charges Solomon to obey God and dies, and Solomon secures his throne by removing Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei.
more: Adonijah asks for Abishag, which Solomon treats as a bid for the throne.
Abiathar is removed from the priesthood and sent to Anathoth.
Shimei breaks his oath by leaving Jerusalem and is executed.

3.line: God offers Solomon whatever he asks, Solomon asks for wisdom, and he shows it by settling two prostitutes' dispute.
more: Solomon marries Pharaoh's daughter, and the people sacrifice at high places.
God also promises riches and honor.
Solomon orders the baby divided, revealing the true mother by her response.

4.line: Solomon's officials and district governors are listed, and his kingdom is described as prosperous and peaceful.
more: Judah and Israel are as many as the sand and eat and drink happily.
Solomon's wisdom surpasses all others, and he speaks thousands of proverbs and songs.

5.line: Solomon arranges with Hiram of Tyre for cedar and cypress timber and organizes laborers to build the temple.
more: David could not build because of constant wars.
Solomon pays Hiram yearly in wheat and oil.
Large stones are cut and prepared for the foundation.

6.line: Solomon builds the temple over seven years, with its structure, cedar paneling, gold overlay, and Most Holy Place described.
more: Construction begins 480 years after the exodus, in Solomon's fourth year.
God promises to dwell among Israel if Solomon obeys.
Two olivewood cherubim stand in the inner sanctuary.

7.line: Solomon builds his palace complex, and Hiram the craftsman makes the bronze pillars, sea, stands, and temple furnishings.
more: The palace takes thirteen years to build.
The two pillars are named Jachin and Boaz.
Solomon brings in the silver and gold David had dedicated.

8.line: The ark is brought into the temple, God's glory fills it, and Solomon offers a long prayer of dedication.
more: Solomon asks God to hear prayers made toward this house, even from exile.
He blesses the people and offers huge sacrifices.
The celebration lasts fourteen days.

9.line: God answers Solomon's prayer, warning that disobedience will bring the temple's destruction, and Solomon's other achievements are described.
more: Hiram is displeased with the twenty cities Solomon gives him.
Solomon uses forced labor, builds cities, and launches a fleet of ships.

10.line: The queen of Sheba visits and marvels at Solomon's wisdom and wealth, which are described in detail.
more: She tests him with hard questions and praises the LORD.
Silver becomes as common as stone in Jerusalem.
Solomon gathers many chariots and horses, including from Egypt.

11.line: Solomon's foreign wives turn his heart to other gods, and God raises adversaries and promises ten tribes to Jeroboam.
more: Solomon has seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines.
Hadad of Edom and Rezon of Damascus oppose him.
The prophet Ahijah tears a cloak into twelve pieces, and Solomon dies after reigning forty years.

12.line: Rehoboam rejects the people's plea for relief, the ten northern tribes make Jeroboam king, and Jeroboam sets up golden calves.
more: Rehoboam follows the young men's harsh advice instead of the elders'.
A prophet forbids Rehoboam to fight Israel.
Jeroboam places calves at Bethel and Dan and appoints priests who are not Levites.

13.line: A man of God from Judah condemns Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, but later disobeys God and is killed by a lion.
more: He predicts a king named Josiah will burn priests' bones on it.
Jeroboam's hand withers and the altar splits apart.
An old prophet deceives him into eating, and Jeroboam continues his evil ways.

14.line: Ahijah foretells disaster on Jeroboam's house, and Rehoboam's Judah falls into idolatry and is plundered by Shishak of Egypt.
more: Jeroboam's wife visits Ahijah in disguise, and their son dies as foretold.
Judah does evil, with high places, pillars, and male cult prostitutes.
Shishak takes the temple treasures, including Solomon's gold shields.

15.line: Abijam does evil and Asa does right in Judah, while Nadab and Baasha do evil in Israel.
more: Asa removes cult prostitutes and idols and deposes his grandmother Maacah.
Asa pays Ben-hadad of Syria to attack Baasha.
Baasha kills Nadab and wipes out Jeroboam's house.

16.line: Israel's kings Elah, Zimri, Omri, and Ahab do evil, with Ahab marrying Jezebel and promoting Baal worship.
more: Zimri kills Elah but reigns only seven days.
Omri buys the hill of Samaria and builds his capital there.
Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost of his sons, as Joshua had said.

17.line: Elijah announces a drought to Ahab, and God provides for Elijah through ravens and a widow at Zarephath.
more: Elijah drinks from the brook Cherith until it dries up.
The widow's flour and oil do not run out.
Elijah raises the widow's son from the dead.

18.line: Elijah defeats the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel when God sends fire, and then the drought ends.
more: Obadiah had hidden a hundred prophets from Jezebel.
Elijah challenges the people to stop wavering between two opinions.
The prophets of Baal are killed, and Elijah prays for rain.

19.line: Elijah flees Jezebel to Horeb, where God speaks in a low whisper and sends him to anoint successors.
more: An angel feeds Elijah in the wilderness.
God says seven thousand in Israel have not bowed to Baal.
Elijah calls Elisha, who leaves his oxen to follow him.

20.line: God gives Ahab two victories over Ben-hadad of Syria, but a prophet condemns Ahab for sparing him.
more: The Syrians claim the LORD is a god of the hills only.
Ahab makes a treaty with Ben-hadad and lets him go.
Ahab goes home sullen and angry.

21.line: Jezebel arranges Naboth's murder so Ahab can take his vineyard, and Elijah pronounces doom on Ahab's house.
more: Naboth refuses to sell his family inheritance.
Elijah says dogs will lick Ahab's blood and eat Jezebel.
Ahab humbles himself, so God delays the disaster until his son's days.

22.line: Ignoring Micaiah's warning, Ahab dies in battle at Ramoth-gilead, while Jehoshaphat reigns in Judah and does right.
more: Ahab's four hundred prophets promise victory, but Micaiah foresees defeat.
Ahab disguises himself, but a randomly shot arrow kills him.
Ahaziah succeeds Ahab in Israel and does evil, serving Baal.

2 Kings.line: Israel and Judah decline under mostly evil kings until Assyria destroys Israel and Babylon destroys Jerusalem and exiles Judah.
more: Elijah is taken to heaven, and Elisha performs many miracles in Israel.
Jehu wipes out Ahab's house and Baal worship, but Israel keeps Jeroboam's golden calves.
Assyria conquers Samaria and exiles Israel because of persistent idolatry.
In Judah, Hezekiah trusts God against Assyria, but Manasseh's great evil seals Judah's fate.
Josiah's reforms do not avert judgment, and Babylon destroys Jerusalem and the temple.
The book ends with exiled King Jehoiachin released from prison in Babylon.

1.line: King Ahaziah of Israel consults Baal-zebub after a fall, and Elijah announces he will die.
more: Fire from heaven consumes two captains and their fifty men sent to seize Elijah.
The third captain pleads for mercy, and Elijah goes with him.
Ahaziah dies, and his brother Jehoram succeeds him.

2.line: Elijah is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, and Elisha receives a double portion of his spirit.
more: Elijah strikes the Jordan with his cloak, and they cross on dry ground.
Elisha heals Jericho's water with salt.
Bears maul boys who jeer at Elisha near Bethel.

3.line: Israel, Judah, and Edom march against rebellious Moab, and God provides water and victory through Elisha.
more: Jehoram of Israel does evil, though not as much as Ahab.
Elisha helps for the sake of Jehoshaphat of Judah.
The king of Moab sacrifices his son on the wall, and Israel withdraws.

4.line: Elisha multiplies a widow's oil, raises the Shunammite woman's son, purifies poisoned stew, and feeds a hundred men.
more: The oil fills every borrowed jar, paying the widow's debt.
The Shunammite had been promised a son for her hospitality.
Twenty loaves feed a hundred men with food left over.

5.line: Naaman the Syrian commander is healed of leprosy by washing in the Jordan, and Gehazi is struck with it for greed.
more: A captive Israelite girl tells Naaman's wife about the prophet in Samaria.
Naaman washes seven times and confesses that Israel's God is the only God.
Gehazi secretly takes silver and clothing from Naaman and lies to Elisha.

6.line: Elisha makes an axe head float and blinds a Syrian army, and Samaria later suffers famine under siege.
more: Elisha reveals Syria's plans, and his servant sees horses and chariots of fire.
Elisha leads the blinded army into Samaria and has them fed and released.
Mothers resort to eating their children, and the king blames Elisha.

7.line: God scatters the Syrian army besieging Samaria, and lepers discover the abandoned camp, ending the famine.
more: Elisha predicts food will be cheap by the next day.
God makes the Syrians hear the sound of a great army, and they flee.
The officer who doubted is trampled at the gate.

8.line: The Shunammite's land is restored, Hazael murders Ben-hadad and becomes king, and evil kings reign in Judah.
more: Elisha weeps, foreseeing the harm Hazael will do to Israel.
Jehoram of Judah marries Ahab's daughter and does evil, and Edom revolts.
His son Ahaziah also does evil.

9.line: Elisha has Jehu anointed king, and Jehu kills King Joram of Israel, King Ahaziah of Judah, and Jezebel.
more: Jehu is commissioned to strike down Ahab's house.
Joram's body is thrown onto Naboth's plot of ground.
Jezebel is thrown from a window, and dogs eat her as Elijah foretold.

10.line: Jehu destroys Ahab's descendants and the worshipers of Baal, but keeps Jeroboam's golden calves.
more: Seventy sons of Ahab are killed in Samaria.
Jehu gathers Baal's worshipers in their temple and has them killed.
God begins to cut off parts of Israel through Hazael.

11.line: Athaliah seizes Judah's throne by killing the royal family, but the priest Jehoiada crowns the hidden child Joash.
more: Jehosheba hides Joash in the temple for six years.
Athaliah is executed, and the house of Baal is torn down.
Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people.

12.line: Joash does right while Jehoiada instructs him and repairs the temple, but pays off Hazael with its treasures.
more: Offerings are collected in a chest beside the altar.
The high places are not removed.
Joash is killed by his servants.

13.line: Jehoahaz and Jehoash of Israel do evil, and the dying Elisha promises limited victories over Syria.
more: God gives Israel a savior from Syrian oppression.
Jehoash strikes the ground only three times with arrows.
A dead man touches Elisha's bones and comes back to life.

14.line: Amaziah of Judah does right but foolishly challenges Israel, while Jeroboam II restores Israel's borders.
more: Amaziah defeats Edom, then Jehoash of Israel defeats him and breaks Jerusalem's wall.
Amaziah is assassinated, and his son Azariah succeeds him.
Jeroboam II does evil, yet God saves Israel through him, as Jonah prophesied.

15.line: Azariah reigns long in Judah, while Israel suffers rapid assassinations and Assyrian invasion under evil kings.
more: Azariah does right but is struck with leprosy.
Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah reign in Israel.
Tiglath-pileser takes territory and exiles people, and Jotham does right in Judah.

16.line: Ahaz of Judah does evil, burns his son as an offering, and seeks Assyria's help, copying a foreign altar.
more: Syria and Israel attack Jerusalem but cannot conquer it.
Ahaz pays tribute to Tiglath-pileser, who captures Damascus.
Uriah the priest builds a copy of the altar Ahaz saw in Damascus.

17.line: Assyria captures Samaria and exiles Israel, because the people persistently worshiped other gods and rejected God's prophets.
more: Hoshea, Israel's last king, seeks help from Egypt and is imprisoned.
Assyria resettles foreigners in Samaria, who mix worship of the LORD with their own gods.
The text lists Israel's sins and God's repeated warnings.

18.line: Hezekiah does right and trusts the LORD, but Assyria invades Judah and its envoy mocks God at Jerusalem.
more: Hezekiah removes high places and breaks the bronze serpent.
He pays Sennacherib tribute, but Assyria still sends an army.
The Rabshakeh urges the people not to trust Hezekiah or the LORD.

19.line: Hezekiah prays, Isaiah promises deliverance, and the angel of the LORD strikes down the Assyrian army.
more: Sennacherib sends a threatening letter, which Hezekiah spreads before the LORD.
God says Assyria's pride will be punished and Jerusalem defended.
Sennacherib returns home and is killed by his sons.

20.line: God heals Hezekiah and adds fifteen years, but Isaiah foretells Babylonian exile after Hezekiah shows envoys his treasures.
more: The shadow moves back ten steps as a sign.
Hezekiah is relieved there will be peace in his own days.
Hezekiah dies, and his son Manasseh succeeds him.

21.line: Manasseh and his son Amon do great evil, and God declares that Jerusalem will be destroyed for it.
more: Manasseh rebuilds high places, builds altars for Baal and the stars, and burns his son.
He sheds much innocent blood in Jerusalem.
Amon is assassinated after two years, and Josiah becomes king.

22.line: Josiah does right and repairs the temple, the Book of the Law is found, and Huldah the prophetess confirms coming judgment.
more: Josiah tears his clothes on hearing the law read.
Huldah says disaster will come, but not in Josiah's lifetime because he humbled himself.

23.line: Josiah renews the covenant and purges idolatry but dies at Megiddo, and Judah's next kings do evil.
more: He destroys high places, including Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, as prophesied.
Judah keeps a Passover unlike any since the days of the judges.
Pharaoh Neco kills Josiah, deposes Jehoahaz, and installs Jehoiakim.

24.line: Babylon subdues Judah, and Nebuchadnezzar takes King Jehoiachin, the treasures, and leading people into exile.
more: Jehoiakim does evil and rebels against Babylon.
God sends raiders against Judah for the sins of Manasseh.
Zedekiah is made king, does evil, and rebels.

25.line: Babylon destroys Jerusalem and the temple, exiles the people, and later releases Jehoiachin from prison.
more: Zedekiah is captured, his sons are killed, and he is blinded.
Gedaliah is appointed governor but is assassinated, and many flee to Egypt.
Evil-merodach gives Jehoiachin a regular place at his table.

1 Chronicles.line: This book traces Israel's genealogies from Adam and retells David's reign, highlighting the ark, God's covenant, and temple preparations.
more: Chapters 1–9 trace genealogies from Adam through Israel's tribes, centering on Judah, David, and Levi.
Saul's death leads to David's anointing over all Israel and the capture of Jerusalem.
David brings the ark to Jerusalem with joyful worship, and God promises him a lasting dynasty.
After victories and a sinful census, David chooses the site for the temple.
David gathers materials, organizes priests, Levites, musicians, and officials, and charges Solomon to build the temple.

1.line: Genealogies trace humanity from Adam through Noah's sons to Abraham, then Ishmael, Esau, and Edom's kings.
more: The list sets Israel within the wider family of nations.
It narrows from all peoples to Abraham's line through Isaac.

2.line: The genealogy of Israel's sons begins, focusing on Judah's line, including Jesse and his son David.
more: Israel's twelve sons are named first.
Judah's descendants include Perez, Hezron, Ram, and Caleb.
Achar is noted for breaking faith over devoted things.

3.line: David's sons are listed, followed by the kings of Judah from Solomon to the exile and beyond.
more: Sons born at Hebron and Jerusalem are named.
The royal line continues through Jehoiachin to Zerubbabel and later descendants.

4.line: Further descendants of Judah and the tribe of Simeon are listed, with brief notes on their towns and conquests.
more: Jabez prays for blessing, and God grants his request.
Simeonites take new pastureland and defeat remaining Amalekites.

5.line: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh, the tribes east of the Jordan, are listed, along with their exile by Assyria.
more: Reuben lost his birthright for defiling his father's bed, and it passed to Joseph.
They won battles when they cried to God, but later were unfaithful.

6.line: Levi's descendants are listed, including the high priests, temple musicians, and the cities given to the Levites.
more: The high priestly line runs from Aaron to the exile.
David appointed Heman, Asaph, and Ethan to lead music.
Only Aaron's descendants offer sacrifices and make atonement.

7.line: The genealogies of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, the other half of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher are listed.
more: Many entries count mighty warriors for military service.
Ephraim's line leads to Joshua son of Nun.

8.line: Benjamin's genealogy is given in more detail, leading to the family of King Saul.
more: Saul's line is traced through Jonathan and his descendants.
Many Benjaminites lived in Jerusalem.

9.line: The people who resettled Jerusalem after exile are listed, including priests, Levites, and gatekeepers, followed by Saul's genealogy again.
more: Judah had been exiled to Babylon for unfaithfulness.
Gatekeepers and Levites guard the temple and care for its utensils and bread.
Saul's line is repeated to introduce the narrative that follows.

10.line: Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa, and the LORD turns the kingdom over to David.
more: The Philistines fasten Saul's head in the temple of Dagon.
Saul died for his unfaithfulness and for consulting a medium instead of the LORD.

11.line: David is anointed king over all Israel at Hebron, captures Jerusalem, and his mighty men are listed.
more: Joab becomes chief by leading the attack on the Jebusites.
Three warriors bring David water from Bethlehem, which he pours out to the LORD.

12.line: Warriors from every tribe join David, first at Ziklag and then at Hebron, to make him king.
more: Benjaminites, Gadites, and men of Judah join him while he hides from Saul.
Clothed by the Spirit, Amasai declares peace to David and his helpers.
Israel feasts three days at Hebron with great joy.

13.line: David tries to bring the ark to Jerusalem on a cart, but Uzzah dies for touching it.
more: All the assembly agrees to bring up the ark.
David leaves it with Obed-edom, whose household is blessed.

14.line: Hiram builds David a palace, David's family grows, and God gives him victory over the Philistines twice.
more: David inquires of God before each battle.
David's fame spreads, and the LORD brings fear of him on the nations.

15.line: David brings the ark to Jerusalem properly, with Levites carrying it and singers and musicians celebrating.
more: David says the earlier failure came from not seeking God as prescribed.
Michal despises David as he dances.

16.line: David places the ark in its tent, appoints Levites for worship, and a song of thanks is sung.
more: Asaph and his brothers lead the praise.
The song draws on several psalms, calling the nations to give thanks.
Zadok serves at the tabernacle in Gibeon.

17.line: God tells David through Nathan that his son will build the temple, and promises David an everlasting dynasty.
more: David may not build the house himself.
David humbly thanks God for his promise.

18.line: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Syria, and Edom, and his officials are listed.
more: David dedicates the spoils to the LORD.
He administers justice and equity to all his people.

19.line: The Ammonites humiliate David's envoys and hire Syrian forces, and Joab and David defeat them.
more: Hanun shaves the envoys and cuts their garments.
The Syrians make peace and stop helping the Ammonites.

20.line: Joab captures Rabbah, and David's men kill several Philistine giants from Gath.
more: David takes the crown of the Ammonite king.
Elhanan kills Lahmi, the brother of Goliath.

21.line: Satan incites David to number Israel, God sends a plague, and David buys Ornan's threshing floor for an altar.
more: Joab objects but obeys, though he leaves out Levi and Benjamin.
God answers David's sacrifice with fire from heaven.
The place becomes the site for the temple.

22.line: David gathers materials for the temple and charges Solomon and Israel's leaders to build it.
more: David may not build because he shed much blood.
Solomon will be a man of rest and peace.

23.line: In his old age David makes Solomon king and organizes the Levites by clans and duties.
more: The Levites are counted and assigned to temple service, officials, gatekeeping, and music.
Their work shifts from carrying the tabernacle to serving in the temple.

24.line: The priests descended from Aaron are divided by lot into twenty-four divisions, and the remaining Levites are also assigned.
more: Both Eleazar's and Ithamar's lines are included.
Lots are cast equally for family heads and younger brothers.

25.line: David appoints the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to prophesy with music in twenty-four divisions.
more: Two hundred eighty-eight trained musicians are counted.
Lots are cast for duties, small and great alike.

26.line: The gatekeepers, treasurers, and Levitical officials outside the temple are assigned their posts.
more: Gates are assigned by lot.
Some Levites oversee dedicated treasures, and others serve as officers and judges.

27.line: Israel's military divisions, tribal leaders, and David's royal officials are listed.
more: Twelve divisions of twenty-four thousand each serve one month a year.
David did not count those under twenty, and Joab's census was not finished.

28.line: David assembles Israel's leaders, charges Solomon to obey God and build the temple, and gives him the plans.
more: David says God chose Solomon to sit on the throne.
David says the plans came to him in writing from the LORD.

29.line: David and the people give generously for the temple, David praises God, Solomon is made king, and David dies.
more: David acknowledges that everything comes from God.
Solomon is anointed a second time, and Zadok as priest.
David reigned forty years over Israel.
